<!--
NUMBER PENDING, as for the other rebuilt supplements.

WHAT THIS IS FOR, and it is the figure the Mahalanobis ones cannot be. A squared Mahalanobis
distance sums over every parameter direction, so it reports the AVERAGE of the distortion matrix's
eigenvalues and nothing else. Measured for IR at ten channels: the eigenvalues run 1.687, 1.138,
1.053, 0.999, 0.936, 0.827 -- a factor two between the best-behaved direction and the worst -- and
their average is 1.11. One direction whose error bar is too small by a factor sqrt(1.687) = 1.30
becomes an eleven per cent effect once it is divided by six, which is half a band width. The
quantile-quantile figures were therefore not contradicting the maps; they were the wrong
instrument, and this is the right one.

THE IDENTITY BEING TESTED. Whiten the cloud with the Fisher the algorithm reports,
Z = F^(1/2)(theta_hat - theta_bar). If the estimator's true covariance is the sandwich
F^-1 J F^-1, then

    Cov(Z) = F^(1/2) F^-1 J F^-1 F^(1/2) = F^(-1/2) J F^(-1/2) = IDM

exactly. So the whitened cloud's covariance IS the distortion matrix, and projecting it onto the
IDM's own eigenvectors must give back the IDM's eigenvalues. That is a six-number prediction per
cell, from the model, against six measurements, from the simulations, with nothing fitted between
them.

WHAT A PANEL SHOWS. One point per (noise level, eigendirection): the eigenvalue the battery's
distortion matrix predicts on the horizontal axis, the variance the whitened cloud actually has
along that direction on the vertical. Six noise levels times six directions is thirty-six points
spanning roughly 0.7 to 1.7, which is a calibration plot and not a single comparison. On the
identity means the distortion matrix is right; the spread around it is what a hundred fits per
cloud can resolve, and the grey guide is that: plus and minus two standard errors of a variance,
sqrt(2/n), around the identity.

WHY THE NOISE LEVELS ARE POINTS AND NOT PANELS. Their eigenvectors differ, so they cannot be
pooled into one curve; but each contributes six independent (prediction, measurement) pairs at its
own place on the axis, which is exactly what a calibration plot wants. Fixing the noise would
leave six points per panel and no range.

THE WORST DIRECTION HAS A COMPOSITION, and it is printed in the table at the foot rather than
drawn, because it is a vector and the panel is already carrying thirty-six points. At ten channels
and the longest interval it is k_off -0.87, N_ch -0.42, i +0.25: almost pure closing rate pulling
against the channel number, which is the N*i ridge seen from the parameter side. That is the
combination whose error bar is too small by thirty per cent, and no per-parameter map can name it
because a map reports coordinates and this is a rotation.

A HUNDRED FITS PER CLOUD, group size 100, converged fits only. The standard error of an empirical
variance is then sqrt(2/99) = 14 per cent, which is the width of the guide. Individual points are
not conclusive; thirty-six of them lying along the identity are.

GROUP SIZE 10 WOULD GIVE A THOUSAND FITS AND IS NOT USED, and this was tested rather than assumed.
Median measured-over-predicted at the two group sizes, same cells:

    N_ch 10, noise 0.1     1.033 (gs 10)   1.018 (gs 100)
    N_ch 10, noise 1       1.116           0.964
    N_ch 20, noise 1       1.050           1.001
    N_ch 100, noise 1      1.028           0.983

With six thousand values against seven hundred the median carries about two per cent, so 1.116
against 0.964 is a seven-sigma disagreement and not sampling. The bias runs one way, three to
twelve per cent upward, and grows as channels are removed: at ten recordings per estimate the MLE
has not reached the regime the sandwich describes and its cloud is wider than the asymptotics
predict. Three times the resolution bought with a systematic artefact the size of the effect is
not a trade worth making. The project's own warning about small group sizes at few channels is
about a sign reversal in the channel-number direction; this is a second face of it, on a quantity
that is blind to the mean.

THE ROWS ARE THE FEW-CHANNEL CORNER, 10 to 100, and not the decade ladder. Above a thousand
channels IR's distortion is gone -- the predicted eigenvalues span 0.85 to 1.24 -- so the
horizontal axis has no range and the calibration plot degenerates: the first version measured a
regression slope of 0.6 there, which is a statement about the lever arm and not about the model.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(data.table); library(ggplot2) })
```

```{r data}
SRC  <- "../figure_4_source_data/figure_4_source_data_eigendirections.csv"
A    <- "macro_IR"
# the few-channel corner, which is where there is distortion to predict at all: at a thousand
# channels and above the predicted eigenvalues collapse into 0.85 to 1.24 and the plot has no
# lever arm left, so those rows measured a regression slope of 0.6 that says nothing about the
# model and everything about the range.
NCHS <- c(10, 20, 50, 100)
ZS   <- c("0.05", "0.1", "0.2", "0.5", "1", "10")
GS   <- 100
PN   <- c("k_on", "k_off", "i", "sigma", "base", "N_ch")
IDMP <- "Probit_statistics_Likelihood_Gaussian_Information_Distortion"
FCVP <- "Probit_statistics_Gaussian_Fisher_Covariance"
.f <- function(n, z, kind)
  Sys.glob(file.path("../data", "*",
                     sprintf("figure_3_G_nch_%d_nsim_10000_%s_noise_%s_%s.csv", n, A, z, kind)))

stamp <- local({
  fs <- unlist(lapply(NCHS, function(n) unlist(lapply(ZS, function(z)
    c(.f(n, z, "mle_cloud_runs"), .f(n, z, "battery_pool_G"))))))
  i <- file.info(c(fs, "figure_4_supplement_eigendirections.Rmd"))
  sprintf("# figure_4 eigendirections | files=%d bytes=%.0f newest=%.0f", length(fs),
          sum(i$size, na.rm = TRUE), max(as.numeric(i$mtime), na.rm = TRUE))
})

# symmetric square root, used to whiten the cloud with the reported Fisher
sqrtm <- function(S) { e <- eigen((S + t(S)) / 2, symmetric = TRUE)
                       e$vectors %*% diag(sqrt(pmax(e$values, 0))) %*% t(e$vectors) }

eig_cell <- function(n, z) {
  fc <- .f(n, z, "mle_cloud_runs"); fb <- .f(n, z, "battery_pool_G")
  if (!length(fc) || !length(fb)) return(NULL)
  d <- fread(fc[1], skip = 1, showProgress = FALSE)
  b <- fread(fb[1], skip = 1, showProgress = FALSE)
  mat <- function(cp, dl, pid) {
    g <- b[component_path == cp & statistic == "value" & probit == "mean" &
           abs(interval_in_tau - dl) < 1e-9 & param_index %in% pid & param_col %in% pid]
    if (!nrow(g)) return(NULL)
    S <- matrix(NA_real_, length(pid), length(pid))
    S[cbind(match(g$param_index, pid), match(g$param_col, pid))] <- g$value
    if (anyNA(S)) NULL else S
  }
  rbindlist(lapply(sort(unique(d$interval_in_tau)), function(dl) {
    cv <- d[variable == "Convergence_Status_Code" & group_size == GS & interval_in_tau == dl]
    ok <- if (nrow(cv)) cv$sample_index[cv$value == 0] else NULL
    TH <- d[variable == "Model_Parameters_Hat" & group_size == GS & interval_in_tau == dl &
            (is.null(ok) | sample_index %in% ok)]
    if (!nrow(TH)) return(NULL)
    W <- dcast(TH, sample_index ~ param_index, value.var = "value")
    M <- as.matrix(W[, -1]); if (nrow(M) < 20) return(NULL)
    pid <- as.integer(colnames(M))
    Fc <- mat(FCVP, dl, pid); Id <- mat(IDMP, dl, pid)
    if (is.null(Fc) || is.null(Id)) {
      cat(sprintf("    SKIP N_ch %d noise %s Delta %g: matrix missing\n", n, z, dl)); return(NULL) }
    # Cov(Z) = IDM exactly, with Z the cloud whitened by the GROUP's reported Fisher
    Z  <- sweep(M, 2, colMeans(M), "-") %*% sqrtm(solve(Fc / GS))
    e  <- eigen((Id + t(Id)) / 2, symmetric = TRUE)
    pr <- Z %*% e$vectors
    top <- e$vectors[, 1]
    data.table(nch = n, z = z, dlt = dl, rank = seq_along(e$values), nfit = nrow(M),
               pred = e$values, obs = apply(pr, 2, var),
               top_lab = paste(sprintf("%s%+.2f", PN[pid + 1], top), collapse = " "))
  }))
}

if (file.exists(SRC) && identical(readLines(SRC, n = 1), stamp)) {
  cat("eigendirections: source CSV is current, reading it\n")
  E <- as.data.table(read.csv(SRC, skip = 1))
} else {
  cat("eigendirections: sweeping\n")
  E <- rbindlist(lapply(NCHS, function(n) rbindlist(lapply(ZS, function(z) {
    r <- eig_cell(n, z)
    if (!is.null(r) && nrow(r)) cat(sprintf("  N_ch %-6d noise %-5s  %d directions\n",
                                            n, z, nrow(r)))
    r
  }))))
  dir.create(dirname(SRC), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  writeLines(stamp, SRC)
  suppressWarnings(write.table(E, SRC, sep = ",", row.names = FALSE, col.names = TRUE,
                               append = TRUE, qmethod = "double"))
}
DLTS <- sort(unique(E$dlt))
E[, nchf := factor(sprintf("N[ch]==%d", nch), levels = sprintf("N[ch]==%d", NCHS))]
E[, dltf := factor(sprintf("Delta==%g", dlt), levels = sprintf("Delta==%g", DLTS))]
cat(sprintf("%d points over %d panels, %d fits per cloud\n", nrow(E),
            uniqueN(E[, .(nch, dlt)]), round(mean(E$nfit))))
```

```{r plot, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 4.6}
GUIDE <- data.table(x = seq(0.5, 2.2, length.out = 100))
GUIDE[, `:=`(lo = x * (1 - 2 * sqrt(2 / 99)), hi = x * (1 + 2 * sqrt(2 / 99)))]
g <- ggplot(E, aes(pred, obs)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = GUIDE, aes(x = x, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              fill = "grey85", colour = NA) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "#1A9850", linewidth = .35) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = factor(rank)), size = .7, alpha = .85) +
  facet_grid(nchf ~ dltf) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.7, 1, 1.5)) + scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.7, 1, 1.5, 2)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.6, 2.0), ylim = c(0.55, 2.4)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#08306B", "#2171B5", "#6BAED6",
                                 "#BDBDBD", "#FDAE61", "#D73027"),
                      name = "direction,\nworst first") +
  labs(x = "eigenvalue the distortion matrix predicts",
       y = "variance the whitened cloud has") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "right",
        legend.key.size = unit(8, "pt"), strip.text = element_text(size = 6.5),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 6.5), axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6.5), legend.title = element_text(size = 6.5))
g
ggsave("Figure_4_supplement_eigendirections.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = 4.6)
```

```{r numbers}
fit <- E[, .(n = .N, slope = coef(lm(log(obs) ~ log(pred)))[2],
             med_ratio = median(obs / pred)), by = .(nch)]
knitr::kable(fit, digits = 3,
             caption = "prediction against measurement: a slope of one and a ratio of one mean the distortion matrix is right")

knitr::kable(unique(E[rank == 1 & dlt == 1, .(nch, z, worst = round(pred, 3), top_lab)]),
             caption = "the worst direction and its composition, at the longest interval")
```
